description.narrative:
Insatsen är i form av stöd till organisationen Women’s Learning Partnership for Rights, Development, and Peace (WLP) som är en koalition bestående av 20 autonoma kvinnorättsorganisationer med ett sekretariat i Bethesda, USA. WLPs partnerorganisationer är baserad i länder över hela det globala syd, med det gemensamma uppdraget att förändra maktrelationer och främja demokrati, jämlikhet, fred och hållbar utveckling.
WLP:s partnerskapsmodell och metodik använder ett decentraliserat, samhällsbaserat tillvägagångssätt för att sprida kunskap om kvinnors rättigheter, demokratiska idéer och metoder, och för att öka WLP:s partners organisatoriska och strategiska möjligheter att påverka beslutsfattande på lokal, nationell, regional och internationell nivå. WLP har tre övergripande målområden för verksamheten i enlighet med deras Strategiska plan, med tydligt definierade uppföljningsbara mål. Målområdena är Ledarskap, mobilisering av kvinnorättsröreslen och stärka det civila samhället

The contribution is in the form of support to the organisation Women’s Learning Partnership for Rights, Development, and Peace (WLP). WLP is an international women’s rights organization comprised of a partnership of 20 autonomous women’s rights organizations, primarily from transitioning and developing societies with WLP’s secretariat located in Maryland, USA. WLP’s mission is to transform power relations and promote justice, equality, peace, and sustainable development by strengthening the feminist movement. This is done through curriculum and resource development, training, capacity development, advocacy and movement building while promoting and sustaining leadership that is participatory and replicable. WLP has three areas of impact. Under each outcome and obejctive there are several goals to be achieved. The three areas of impact are Leadership, Mobilising the women´s movement and Civil society strengthening.

WLP has three areas of impact. Under each outcome and obejctive there are several goals to be achieved (please find more information in the application).
1. Leadership Outcome: FEMINIST LEADERSHIP Empower feminist leaders to fully participate in civic, economic, and political life in the Global South.
Objective 1:WLP will increase womens engagement in the political process and in decisionmaking positions. In four years, more women will be engaged in the political process and in decisionmaking positions in the communities where WLP works and beyond.
Objective 2: WLP will promote the adoption and application of feminist principles to advance rights and justice. In four years, in the communities where WLP works and beyond, leaders are using feminist principles to advance rights and justice in their spheres of influence
Objective 3: WLP will promote and safeguard gender justice. In four years, the communities where WLP works will promote and safeguard gender justice. Objective 4: WLP will empower and mobilize young leaders to advocate for gender justice. In four years, more young leaders will advocate for gender justice in the communities where WLP works and beyond.
2. Movements Outcome: MOBILIZING THE WOMENS MOVEMENT Accelerate movements for justice and ending violence and discrimination against women and girls.In four years:
Objective 1: WLP will educate, train, and mobilize individuals and CSOs to contribute to the success of legal reforms that promote gender justice. In four years, in the communities where WLP works and beyond, there will be successful legal reforms to promote gender justice.
Objective 2: WLP will increase the impact of local, national, and regional women's human rights movements by facilitating greater coordination at the regional level. In four years, in the regions where WLP works, local, national, and regional women's human rights movements will have more impact because of increased coordination at the regional level.
Objective 3: WLP will build capacity and drive greater collaboration among activists and CSOs to collectively advocate for policies that address gender equality, peacebuilding, democratic values, climate justice, and human rights. In four years, CSOs af iliated with WLP partners in their regions will be collaborating with each other and WLP to bring about genderresponsive policies.
Objective 4: WLP will collect, record, and share the important history and accomplishments of women to inspire and catalyze feminist movements around the world. In four years, the history and accomplishments of women in the Global South, particularly from the regions where WLP works, will fuel feminist movements.
3. Civil Society Outcome: CIVIL SOCIETY STRENGTHENING Propel the collective power of womenled civil society organizations to protect and advance democracy, human rights, and gender justice.
Objective 1: WLP will strengthen the capacity of partner organizations in program implementation, organizational development, and mobilization, including to more effectively work in changing or difficult environments. In four years, the organizations that WLP engages with will be more effective in program implementation and more resilient to crisis situations.
Objective 2: WLP will empower civil society organizations to effectively serve as robust defenses against poverty, corruption, authoritarianism, discrimination, and violence. In four years, CSOs in the communities where WLP works and beyond will be able to serve as bulwarks against poverty, corruption, authoritarianism, discrimination, and violence.
Objective 3: WLP will support women's rights activists and leaders operating in regions where civil society faces significant challenges by building and supporting impactful coalitions and movements for women's rights. In four years, human and womens rights activists working for freedom and rights in places where civil society is not able to function will have built efective alliances and movements for rights.

description.narrative:
Examples of results achieved:
The reporting from WLP provides an overview of the key achievements, challenges, lessons learned, and unexpected outcomes of the Womens Learning Partnership (WLP) between July 2024 and June 2025. In FY25, Womens Learning Partnership (WLP) and its partners across the Global South advanced women´s rights and gender justice in a global context marked by shrinking civic space, decreased funding, rising authoritarianism, and climate and humanitarian crises. Despite these challenges, the Partnership strengthened feminist leadership, achieved legal reform outcomes, and bolstered the resilience of civil society organizations (CSOs).
Reach and Leadership Development Examples of results:
Through 12 Training of Trainers (TOT) programs and 58 grassroots workshops, WLP trained 1,632 people, including 732 youth, across 15 countries. Leveraging WLPs multiplier effect methodology, trainees from these programs have conducted stepdown workshops in their communities, reaching an additional 670 women, men, and youth. 95 percent of workshop participants reported an increased awareness of womens rights, while 90 percent saw themselves as leaders and agents of change. As a direct result of WLP trainings, 247 women and youth assumed new leadership roles, and youth-led initiatives, from digital campaigns in Kyrgyzstan to mental health advocacy in Indonesia, demonstrated the next generations active engagement in democratic and social change. In FY25, 78 WLP trained political candidates ran for office in Brazil, Kyrgyzstan, Indonesia, and Pakistan, and 35 were elected to leadership positions. Additionally, the Partnership trained 399 women and men as election monitors and helped 415 women register to vote. (WLP annual report p.14) In May 2025, WLP held its first ever global Alumni Event to launch the WLP´s Alumni network. The intergenerational virtual event brought together leaders, activists, educators, and changemakers from 20 countries around the world who had previously participated in WLPs Global TOT program. More than 100 participants gathered to share stories of how working with the Partnership has impacted their work, shaped their perspectives, and influenced their personal journeys.
Impact of Legal Reforms and Advocacy Examples of results:
The Partnership recorded 159 advocacy outcomes and secured three landmark legal reforms in FY25. These include: - In Pakistan, the Sindh High Court affirmed divorced daughters right to inherit pensions, and parliament passed the Islamabad Child Marriage Restraint Act raising the marriage age to 18. - In Brazil, WLP partner helped secure approval of Resolution 258/2024, strengthening protections for child and adolescent survivors of sexual violence. -In Mauritania, WLP partner trained 75 parliamentarians, catalyzing the creation of a women led parliamentary commission to advance a new personal status code.
Beyond the passage of these new laws, partners influenced policymaking processes in Egypt, Morocco, Malaysia, and Kyrgyzstan, producing draft legislations, mobilizing coalitions, and ensuring that womens voices shaped family law reform, labor protections, and gender responsive governance. At UN CSW, WLP collaborated with Global Campaign for Equality in Family Law (GCEFL) coalition to cohost a CSW side event with the governments of Sweden and Zambia: WLP cohosted The Rise of Family Values: Strategies for Rights Based Family Law Reform to tackle the increasing use of family values rhetoric to justify discrimination, particularly in personal status laws governing marriage, divorce, child custody, and inheritance. WLPs Regional MENA Director spoke about Morocco´s successes and struggles with the reform of the inheritance laws
Examples of results: WLP reported 90 outcomes that directly strengthened CSO capacity, including mentoring emerging organizations, developing cross sectoral partnerships, and fostering resilience in contexts of shrinking civic space.
